claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, who is 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 17, I need to ask a few more questions to determine eligibility.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to Level 3
- A traineeship in England

Please note this does not include higher education (like university degrees) or paid employment of more than 24 hours per week.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in college or doing A-levels or anything like that. He actually started an apprenticeship recently - he's training to be an electrician.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have one more important question about Alex's apprenticeship.

Is Alex's apprenticeship a **paid apprenticeship** (where he receives wages from an employer), or is it an **unpaid traineeship**?

This distinction is important for determining Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's a paid apprenticeship - he gets wages from the company he's working for.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, you would **not** be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

- Alex is 17 years old
- He is not in approved education or approved training
- A **paid apprenticeship** does not count as approved education or training for Child Benefit purposes

Child Benefit for children aged 16-19 is only available if the child remains in approved education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to Level 3, or Scottish Highers) or approved unpaid training (such as a traineeship in England). Since Alex is in a paid apprenticeship where he receives wages, this does not meet the criteria.

Let me record this outcome for you now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry the outcome wasn't what you may have hoped for. To summarise:

**Alex (age 17):** ❌ Not eligible

Because Alex is in a paid apprenticeship rather than approved education or unpaid training, you cannot claim Child Benefit for him.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he were to leave the apprenticeship and return to full-time approved education—you may be able to make a new claim at that point.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
